- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 2022-08-30, 2023-02-13).
- Forecasts show a strong upward trend even when historical data suggests mean reversion or recent declines.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 2023-02-13, 2023-05-08), model fails to correct or overcorrects, leading to overshoots.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — forecasts remain high while true values fall sharply.
- Forecasts tend to be overly smooth, ignoring volatility or sudden reversals in the 30-day history.
- In periods of high volatility (e.g., 2023-05-08–09), model underestimates the magnitude of drops and overestimates recovery.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of the distribution — underestimates extreme lows or overestimates extreme highs.
- Forecasts are generally too optimistic in the short term (1–3 days) and too pessimistic in the long term (10+ days) — suggesting horizon mismatch.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or calendar effects (e.g., May vs. February) — leading to inconsistent behavior across months.
- When true values show a clear downward trend, model continues to project upward, especially if recent history is upward trending.
